data: No details of the stone are recorded, other than its fragmentary state.
Probably later second or early third century CE, due to presence of name T. Aelius
Unearthed along with many other fragments in 'area Stesichori' (i.e. the general area of the amphitheatre on the north side of the city centre) in 1740 according to Amico
Seen by Mommsen, in museo Biscari
Not seen since Mommsen and assumed to be lost.

commentary

Manganaro and Korhonen suggest that this might be a list of officials; Amico assumed it to be a list of those buried in a tomb and so funerary, since the area of its discovery is more broadly that of the necropolis.
